beats.narration_en: Drive over this road and it plays a song.
It's cut with grooves like a giant vinyl record.
Each time a tire hits a groove, it makes a thump.
Hundreds of thumps a second blur into one note.
Close grooves make a high note and wider gaps a lower one.
Space them just right and the road plays a melody.
Drive slower and the song slows down and drops in pitch.
In California, one plays the William Tell Overture.
But the crew measured the gap between grooves, not groove to groove.
So every note came out flat, the high notes most of all.
That's why California's famous musical road is out of tune.
